collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A friend warns a villager not to cross the rocks at high tide: cross anyway, or wait after all.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: "Don't cross the rocks at high tide," says (friend) as (subject) heads off to the far beach. "Wait for low tide. It's safer." (subject) doesn't want to wait two hours. (subject.He/she) goes anyway, carefully, picking (subject.his/her) way over the wet rocks while (friend) watches from the sand with (friend.his/her) arms folded.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) crosses. It's slippery but fine. (subject.He/she) gets a little wet. On the other side (subject.he/she) waves. (friend) waves back, still frowning. Nothing bad happens. That doesn't make (friend)'s advice wrong, and it doesn't make (subject)'s choice wrong either. It just means today the rocks were kind. Both of them understand that perfectly well.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) looks at the rocks, at the water slapping against them, and sighs. "Fine," (subject.he/she) says, and sits down next to (friend). They wait two hours, talking about nothing much. It's actually rather nice. When the tide goes down, (subject) crosses easily. (subject.He/she) doesn't say (friend) was right. (friend) doesn't say it either.
